Most crates have junk.

But I heard a few have gold coins!
Only one way to find out...

I hate when you're right.

We must find out what's inside without opening it.

Ok, kiddo.

Let's find all the 📦 that weigh the same as💰.
And I thought he was born with that cable around his neck...

Because right now, that crate's weight is an unknown value. 

In math, we call that a variable.

No.
x stands in for the crate's weight.
 
Since we don't know its actual value yet, we will call it x for now.

options: a letter that stands for a number we don't know yet

I know that 💰weighs 12.

Let's see how much this crate weighs...

x = 12

It means the crate is full of money... right?
We could have picked <font color="#000000">any letter</font> to <font color="#000000">name</font> the <font color="#000000">variable</font>.

All these crates weigh 12.

Let's get out of here.
Back in the lab...

A variable is a symbol—usually a letter—that stands in for an unknown or changing amount.

Any letter works, though lowercase ‭x‬, ‭y‬, and ‭z‬ are the most common.
